newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower in sluggish dealings.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower in sluggish dealings.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly lower in sluggish dealings but traders said losses were limited by rain-related delays in harvest activity in Texas.
KCBT wheat spent most of the session flip-flopping between positive and negative territory.

"The key today is, there was absolutely no harvest pressure whatsoever, which is very unusual for May 30," a KCBT trader said. "We kept bringing it back because there was no hedge pressure, but at the same time the market was undermined because the funds were leaning on it."

Wheat had opened firmer on bullish export data and on spillover from soybeans. USDA said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended May 22 totaled 928,800 tonnes, above expectations for 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
But futures weakened early and volumes dropped off.
KCBT wheat ended steady to 10 cents per bushel lower, with July down one cent at $3.87-1/2.
Cargill Investor Services was a featured player on the day, bull-spreading 1.5 million July/Sept bushels at 1-1/2 cents. Commission house Refco sold 2.2 million July, traders said.
